decision: Seckin 2026-11-19 12:03 +0300 (relayed by his supervisor 12:05): for heavy work on the laptop (big downloads, builds, installs, clones, admissions) the fixed 30 GiB floor is replaced by the job's own expected footprint plus a 12 GiB margin; the 12 GiB floor for Lambda launches and the Drive auto-pause below 12 GiB stay as they are
read_by: tools/loop/launch_floors.py (disk_problem, margin_gib, lambda_launch_floor_gib), at each call; through it tools/seal_route_driver.py (the seal and admission gates, the route request), tools/loop/resource_reading.py and standing order 14 (tools/loop/standing_orders_check.py)
lambda_launch_floor_source: D-726 (Seckin 18 Nov 12:08): the route request (seal_route_driver.py request, order 91) is refused under 12 GiB free; the route's laptop worst case is 2.5 GiB. Unchanged by the 19 November decision
not_here: the Drive uploader's pause (config/drive_no_download.json upload_pause, 12 GiB) and the disk sweep's own trigger (config/disk_sweep.json, D-611) are separate decisions and read their own files
_why: an unreadable or malformed file never lowers a floor: the readers fall back to the old fixed 30 GiB (D-099) and say so; a job whose footprint is not known is held to that 30 GiB fallback and says so, never to the margin alone
